memos.headline: AAPL and GOOGL Lead Relative Strength; UNH and PG in Structural Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of 2025-11-14. AAPL sits just 1% off its 52-week high with an RSI of 64.8 and +15.4% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks — this is a textbook trend-following setup, though the +6.4% extension above the 50d mean warrants tight trailing stops near 256 (the approximate 50d level). GOOGL is the standout momentum name, up 38.4% over 12 weeks with +32.7% relative strength vs SPY, but at +40.3% above its 200d mean it is extremely stretched and I'd want to see a pullback toward the 50d area (~257) before adding. On the other side, UNH is in a severe structural downtrend — 47.3% off its 52-week high, 14.5% below its 200d mean, RSI 37.4 — and I see no reason to step in front of that until it can reclaim at least 350. PG is similarly weak with negative 12-week relative strength of -12.7% and price 7.7% below its 200d mean, a clear avoid until it can hold above 155.

views.note: Only 1% off 52w high, strong 12w relative strength of +15.4% vs SPY; would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~256).
Dominant 12w relative strength (+32.7%) but +40% above 200d mean is stretched; a pullback to ~257 (50d area) would be a higher-conviction entry.
Up 32.6% over 12w with +26.9% relative strength vs SPY and RSI 55 — trend is strong but +38.9% above 200d mean is extended; reversal level ~500.
Near highs with only -2.2% drawdown, RSI 63.8, and positive 4w/12w relative strength; would exit on a close below 114 (approximate 50d).
Down 47.3% from 52w high, 14.5% below 200d mean, RSI 37.4 — broken trend with no sign of stabilization; need a reclaim of 350 to reconsider.
Persistent underperformance with -12.7% 12w relative strength vs SPY and price below both moving averages; avoid until a close above 155.

Sharp -4% last week offset by strong 4w return; RSI 49.8 and flat 12w relative strength vs SPY suggest no clear edge here.
Slightly below 50d mean with RSI 44.4 and negative 12w relative strength; not broken but not leading — need a close above 320 to get interested.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Lead on Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse Demands Caution
memos.body: I see the strongest durable earnings profiles in NVDA (56.5% net margin, +55.6% YoY revenue growth on just $8.47B total debt) and GOOGL (34.2% net margin, +15.9% revenue growth with only $14.79B debt). MSFT also impresses at 35.7% net margin and 18.4% revenue growth, though net income growth of 12.5% lags the top line, suggesting some cost absorption I want to monitor. The most alarming print is UNH: despite 12.2% revenue growth, net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B, compressing the net margin to just 2.1%—a level that signals structural cost or claims pressure rather than a one-off. On the industrial side, CAT posted 9.5% revenue growth but net income fell 6.7%, pointing to margin headwinds, while XOM saw both revenue (-5.2%) and earnings (-12.3%) decline. I would need to see UNH's medical-loss ratio stabilize and XOM's upstream realizations recover before reconsidering either name.

views.note: 56.5% net margin and 55.6% revenue growth on minimal leverage represent best-in-class earnings power; would reassess if gross margins compress below 70%.
34.2% net margin with 15.9% revenue growth and low $14.79B debt make this a high-quality compounder; net income up 33% YoY outpacing revenue.
18.4% revenue growth and 35.7% net margin are excellent, but net income growth of only 12.5% suggests rising cloud capex is compressing flow-through—watching opex leverage next quarter.
Net income up 38.2% YoY to $21.19B on 13.4% revenue growth shows margin expansion to 11.8%, but $55.1B debt and capex intensity keep my confidence moderate.
Revenue +7.9% and net income +86.4% look strong, but the income jump likely reflects a tough prior-year comp; $90.68B total debt is the highest in the universe ex-JPM.
31% net margin and 11.6% net income growth are solid for a bank, but the macro-sensitive revenue base and $427B debt load limit upside conviction.
Steady 21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are reassuring, but only 3% revenue growth caps the earnings trajectory.
Net income down 61.2% YoY to $2.35B and net margin of just 2.1% signal severe cash-flow compression; I need to see the medical-loss ratio reverse before reconsidering.
Revenue -5.2% and net income -12.3% with an 8.8% net margin reflect commodity headwinds; would reconsider only if upstream realizations materially improve.
Revenue grew 9.5% but net income fell 6.7%, implying margin pressure at 13%; need to see cost discipline before turning constructive.

memos.headline: Fed in Easing Mode but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal a Cautious Late-Cycle Regime
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing cycle — the upper bound has dropped 75bp over the past year to 4.00%, with 50bp of that in the last three months alone. However, headline CPI is running at 3.0% y/y (September print), which is still uncomfortably above target and limits the pace of further cuts. The labor market is softening meaningfully, with unemployment at 4.40%, up 30bp over both three- and twelve-month horizons, consistent with a late-cycle slowdown. The 10y yield at 4.14% has declined 29bp y/y and the 2s10s spread has steepened 36bp to +0.53pp, confirming the market is pricing continued easing but not a deep recession. A CPI print breaking below 2.5% y/y or unemployment jumping above 4.7% would shift my regime call toward aggressive easing, favoring duration and defensives more decisively.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields and continued easing cycle; moderate confidence given sticky inflation could slow the pace of cuts.
Lower long-end rates support equity duration and consumer spending, though 3% CPI and rising unemployment temper the consumer outlook.
Positive 2s10s steepening (+36bp y/y) helps NIM, but the easing cycle compresses short-end yields and rising unemployment raises credit risk.
Late-cycle slowdown signaled by rising unemployment and still-restrictive real rates is unfavorable for cyclicals exposed to capex and construction.
Defensive staples benefit from a late-cycle regime with softening labor market; falling 10y yields provide a modest valuation tailwind.
Slowdown regime typically pressures energy demand, but sticky inflation and geopolitical uncertainty keep me from outright avoiding the name.
High-duration growth equity stands to benefit from declining 10y yields in an easing cycle, though elevated CPI could cap the pace of rate relief.
Consumer-facing growth name benefits from easing financial conditions, but rising unemployment at 4.4% is a headwind to discretionary spending.
Ad-driven revenue is sensitive to the late-cycle slowdown; lower rates help valuation but macro uncertainty keeps me sidelined.
Defensive healthcare is less macro-sensitive; the easing cycle is mildly supportive but I lack strong conviction on direction from macro data alone.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: AMZN and CAT Surged on Results While MSFT and JPM Sold Off — Divergence Signals Selective Opportunity
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. AMZN (+9.6%) and CAT (+11.6%) saw outsized positive reactions to their Q3 results, suggesting the market was positioned too negatively heading into prints — a classic tone-turning-up-from-low-expectations setup that can carry momentum. Conversely, MSFT (-2.9%) and JPM (-1.9%) drew negative reactions, indicating crowded expectations or disappointing narratives that may weigh on near-term sentiment. AAPL (-0.4%), XOM (-0.3%), PG (+0.2%), and UNH (+0.5%) all had muted reactions, suggesting their earnings were largely priced in and offer no clear sentiment edge. UNH's flurry of non-earnings filings (Reg FD on 11/7, bylaws amendment on 11/13) adds governance noise that I'd watch but doesn't shift the tone materially.

views.note: The +9.6% post-earnings pop signals a meaningful positive narrative shift from previously cautious positioning, and momentum from such moves tends to persist short-term.
An +11.6% earnings-day move is exceptional for a mega-cap industrial, indicating the market was caught offside bearish — sentiment has room to re-rate further.
The -2.9% post-earnings decline suggests expectations were too high and the narrative has turned cautious; I'd wait for sentiment to trough before re-engaging.
A -1.9% reaction to Q3 results plus multiple follow-on filings without a recovery signal suggest sentiment remains soft, though the move is modest enough that conviction is limited.
A near-flat -0.4% earnings reaction implies the result was fully priced; no sentiment edge either way.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and subsequent governance filings (bylaws amendment, Reg FD) add noise but no clear directional tone shift.
A +2.5% post-earnings move is modestly positive but not outsized enough to signal a durable narrative shift; the subsequent 11/6 'Other Events' filing adds no clear sentiment catalyst.
Flat -0.3% earnings reaction and routine follow-on filings suggest sentiment is balanced with no edge.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Near Double 3-Month Ago Levels Signals Structural Geopolitical Risk Across Export-Sensitive Names
memos.body: I am flagging a dramatic surge in the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index to 476, up 97% over three months and 19% over the past month alone, alongside a VIX that has risen 38% over the same three-month window to 20. This combination suggests the market is pricing in sustained policy-driven risk—likely tied to trade, sanctions, or export-control escalation—rather than a one-off event. WTI crude at $59.54, down 6.5% over three months, is consistent with demand-side concern or an easing of energy supply fears, which somewhat insulates energy names from the worst geopolitical scenarios but also caps upside. Credit spreads remain contained (HY OAS at 3.09%), so systemic financial stress is not yet evident, but the gap between equity-vol signals and credit calm is a fragility I am watching. I would need to see the uncertainty index retreat below 350 and VIX below 16 to turn constructive on names with heavy China/export-control exposure.

views.note: Highest exposure to export-control and China-policy risk in the universe; the near-doubling of the policy uncertainty index over three months is a direct headwind to semiconductor supply-chain planning.

Supply-chain concentration in China remains a structural vulnerability, but consumer-staple demand characteristics and services mix provide partial offset; staying neutral until policy clarity improves.
Infrastructure spending tailwinds could be offset by tariff and trade-policy uncertainty reflected in the 97% 3-month surge in the EPU index; recent Reg FD disclosure does not resolve the ambiguity.

WTI at $59.54 is soft but contained credit spreads and multiple recent 8-K filings suggest active capital-markets engagement; energy security policy tailwinds could support domestic producers even as crude weakens.
Cloud and AI capex plans face potential export-control headwinds, but diversified revenue and domestic enterprise demand limit downside; policy uncertainty keeps me from going long.
Financials benefit from a positively sloped yield curve (10y-2y at +53bp) and contained HY spreads at 3.09%; sanctions-related compliance revenue is a modest tailwind in a high-uncertainty regime.
